messages:
emily (docs): Quick FYI — I noticed the API reference for POST /v3/embeddings/batch has a couple of issues: the request example uses `batch_size` but the runtime expects `max_batch_tokens`, and the response example omits `input_index`. I'm opening a tiny PR but want to sync before I push.

ajay (sdk): thanks for flagging — we recently changed the internal param name in the v3 client to `max_batch_tokens` to support token-aware batching. the SDK still accepts `batch_size` for backward compat but docs should reflect recommended usage + migration note.

emily (docs): @ajay good to know. can you confirm the canonical param we should show in examples and the header we should call out for migration? i can update the curl + python snippets.

ajay (sdk): canonical = `max_batch_tokens` (int). migration snippet: accept both, but prefer `max_batch_tokens` for throughput tuning. sample: ```js
// v2 style
client.embeddings.create({model: "rwd-embed-1", inputs: [...], batch_size: 16})
// v3 preferred
client.embeddings.create({model: "rwd-embed-1", inputs: [...], max_batch_tokens: 4096})
```

matt (eng): also saw that the response example in docs shows `data: [ { embedding: [...], id: "abc" } ]` — runtime actually includes `input_index` to map inputs to outputs when the server reorders or compresses batches. missing field caused a support ticket yesterday. please add `input_index` and a short note about reordering.

emily (docs): ok i'll add `input_index` and a sentence: "Note: server may reorder inputs for batching; use `input_index` to map outputs to original inputs." any preferred wording?

sofia (product): +1 on including the migration blurb. maybe call out perf tradeoffs: switching to `max_batch_tokens` lets us pack variable-length inputs more efficiently, so recommend testing with a few workloads. small note under "Performance" section.

ajay (sdk): one more SDK snippet tweak: our Python SDK has both params in the function signature as kwargs with `max_batch_tokens` last — docs should show explicit kwarg names to avoid confusion. example: ```py
# python
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="rwd-embed-1", inputs=["a","b"], max_batch_tokens=4096)
```

emily (docs): thanks. i'll update curl, python, and js snippets, add the migration note (v2 -> v3) and the response example with `input_index`. also will add a small code block showing how to handle reordering when mapping outputs back to inputs: ```py
# map outputs back to original order
outputs = sorted(resp.data, key=lambda x: x['input_index'])
embeddings = [o['embedding'] for o in outputs]
```

emily (docs): opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1290 — contains example fixes and a short migration section. requesting review from @ajay and @matt.

ajay (sdk): looking now. quick nit: in the JS snippet please prefer named param object instead of positional args to avoid confusion with older clients. otherwise LGTM.

matt (eng): will check the `input_index` example against runtime behavior and confirm the field name/position. if we change shape, i'll ping here.

deploy-bot: New PR deployed to staging docs preview: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/batch (auto-preview for PR 1290).

emily (docs): perfect — i'll wait for your confirm then merge. thanks all :thumbsup:
